raw_case_text:
A 30-year-old male from a leprosy-endemic area in West Java, Indonesia, was consulted by a rheumatologist with erythematous plaques covered with thick scales on the face, neck, trunk, back, arms, and lower limbs that were neither itchy nor painful for the last month. The complaint was accompanied by swollen eyelids and painfully swollen fingers on both hands and feet. Approximately two years prior to consulting, there was a palm-sized erythematous macule on the left lower leg with decreased sensation. The skin lesion then increased in number and spread to the face, elbow, back, and epigastric region. Six months prior to consulting, there was increased erythema and thickened macules with thick scales. He visited a general practitioner and was diagnosed with an allergic reaction, then received antiallergy medicines. The complaint subsided, and the skin lesions reverted into hyperpigmented macules. The edematous eyelids and fingers, along with the increased erythema and thickened skin lesions exhibited a recurring pattern, particularly when the patient was tired from work. The patient works as a water heater construction worker, occasionally unintentionally encountering hot materials and water, which resulted in injuries. Psoriasis vulgaris and psoriatic arthritis were diagnosed when the patient consulted a rheumatologist. He was then consulted at a dermatology and venereology clinic at Dr. Hasan Sadikin General Hospital for further evaluation regarding psoriasis vulgaris.
The physical examination showed edema on the eyelids and fingers on both hands and feet (Figure 1A-C), accompanied by painful interphalangeal joints of both hands and feet, without madarosis, ear lobe infiltration, or nail changes. There was decreased sensitivity of annular erythematous macules and annular erythematous plaques with clear inner and outer borders that were covered by psoriasiform scales (Figure 2) on almost the entire part of the body (Figure 1D-F). Auspitz sign was negative. The right great auricular nerve and both common peroneal nerves were observed to have non-tender enlargements with a rubbery consistency. Slit-skin smear examinations from anesthetic psoriasiform plaques on the left arm revealed the presence of acid-fast bacilli (AFB) with an average bacterial index (BI) of 3+ and a morphological index (MI) of 34.8%.
The skin biopsies were done on anesthetic erythematous plaques on both thighs. Histopathological examinations revealed a granulomatous reaction with epithelioid cells, Langhans giant cells, and lymphocyte infiltration (Figure 3) that supported the diagnosis of mid-borderline leprosy. The patient was diagnosed with leprosy with a severe reversal reaction and then treated with multidrug therapy (MDT)-multibacillary (MB) regimen consisting of rifampicin 600 mg and clofazimine 300 mg supervised once a month, dapsone 100 mg and clofazimine 50 mg daily, unsupervised given for 12 months. The patient was also given prednisone 40 mg daily, reduced gradually by 5-10 mg every 2 weeks for the treatment of the reversal reaction. The improvement of eyelids edema, fingers edema (Figure 4A-C), and skin lesions was seen on the 40th day of observation (Figure 4D-F).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 30-year-old male from West Java, Indonesia, presented with a 1-month history of non-pruritic, painless erythematous plaques with thick psoriasiform scales over the face, neck, trunk, and extremities, accompanied by eyelid edema and painful swelling of the fingers and toes.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The illness began 2 years prior with a palm-sized hypoesthetic erythematous macule on the left lower leg that subsequently multiplied and spread to the face, elbows, back, and epigastrium. Six months before presentation, the lesions became increasingly erythematous, thickened, and scaly, accompanied by recurrent eyelid and digital edema triggered by physical fatigue; a general practitioner diagnosed an allergic reaction and prescribed antiallergy medications with transient regression to hyperpigmented macules. One month prior to dermatology referral, generalized thick scaly plaques and painful digital dactylitis recurred, leading a rheumatologist to diagnose psoriasis vulgaris and psoriatic arthritis and refer him for dermatological evaluation.
subjective.past_medical_history: He resided in a leprosy-endemic region of West Java and worked as a water heater construction worker with occasional unintentional thermal burns from hot water and materials.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for eyelid swelling, painful swelling of the fingers and toes, and fatigue-related flares; negative for pruritus or lesional skin pain.

objective.physical_examination: Physical examination demonstrated bilateral eyelid edema, dactylitis/edema of the fingers and toes with tender interphalangeal joints of the hands and feet, and absence of madarosis, earlobe infiltration, or nail changes. Cutaneous examination revealed widespread annular erythematous macules and plaques with sharply demarcated inner and outer borders ('punched-out' configuration), overlying psoriasiform scales, negative Auspitz sign, and decreased cutaneous sensation. Peripheral nerve palpation showed non-tender, rubbery enlargement of the right great auricular nerve and bilateral common peroneal nerves.
objective.advanced_workup: Slit-skin smear (SSS) from anesthetic psoriasiform plaques on the left arm and skin biopsies from anesthetic erythematous plaques on bilateral thighs were performed.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Slit-skin smear revealed acid-fast bacilli with a Bacteriological Index (BI) of 3+ and a Morphological Index (MI) of 34.8%, and thigh skin biopsy histopathology showed epithelioid cell granulomas with Langhans giant cells and lymphocytic infiltration, confirming mid-borderline (BB) leprosy with a severe Type 1 reversal reaction (ruling out psoriasis vulgaris and psoriatic arthritis). The patient was treated with a 12-month WHO multibacillary multidrug therapy (MDT-MB) regimen (monthly supervised rifampicin 600 mg and clofazimine 300 mg, plus daily unsupervised dapsone 100 mg and clofazimine 50 mg) combined with oral prednisone 40 mg daily tapered by 5-10 mg every 2 weeks, resulting in marked resolution of eyelid edema, digital swelling, and psoriasiform plaques by day 40.
